critique: The render has a credible hot white ignition point at 0.08s, but it remains much too small for the intended explosive Fire Trails look. At 2s, the result is dominated by sparse, discrete peach ember blobs on widely separated ballistic arcs. The explosion has expanded so far that its center is mostly empty, and the arcs do not resolve into dense, continuous flame trails. It also lacks the stronger yellow-orange fire body and compact explosive cohesion expected from the preset thumbnail.

suggestions.why: Reduce primary emission velocity so particles remain in a more compact explosive burst instead of spreading into a nearly full-frame field of isolated embers.
Reduce the strong downward ballistic pull so the burst retains radial fire-trail structure rather than becoming falling ember arcs by 2 seconds.
Tighten directional spread enough to form denser visible trail masses while preserving an explosive multi-directional silhouette.
Increase secondary-particle emission density so the existing dotted ember paths connect into fuller, more continuous fiery trails.
Shift the secondary fire color from muted peach toward a hotter saturated orange-red flame appearance.
